finding_and_opportunity_index.label: Cultivation law content is declarative but read by a shared state machine: law loading sorts bottleneck locations, current law selects stages, and positive practice stops at the next fractional threshold until its distinct bottleneck is cleared. Aptitude mismatch changes efficiency rather than proving a universal hard admission gate.

Ordinary seated practice spends the Practice need per dt, gains stage value and tree experience, and restores Rest. Location element/ling, mental and emotional state, mentor effect, building effectiveness, season and event-driver modifiers alter the rate. The practice job prefers an assigned practice building, then room, then map; it can reconsider higher-priority work every five world-time units.

A normal Chance attempt obtains the configured required item, then consumes all configured ResourceCost entries and one item per ItemCost entry on toil entry, drains current Ling, waits CostTime, and attempts the current live chance on leave. The selected law Stage2 furnace bottleneck costs 10 maximum-age units and one Item_Dan_JingYuan2, not merely a possession check.

Chance probability combines configured base plus retry experience, then luck, mind and active medicine/property multipliers, additive sect fengshui/light/weather/season/location factors, retained core-grade modifier, and current consciousness; it clamps to 0..1. Parameters are read when TryBrokenNeck runs, not copied from the earlier preview. Water/metal light bonuses favor lower light; fire/wood favor higher light; earth favors intermediate light.

Failure is a stateful outcome: retry count increments, configured body damage is rolled, failure mood/modifier may persist, a configured non-Chance timestamp resets, and depleted stage value can move the actor back below the gate. The reviewed normal leave/failure path contains no refund for the entry-consumed items or maximum age. Success clears TouchNeck/retry count, applies rewards and can advance stage; stage advance reactivates equipment and informs difficulty.

Golden-core formation is a finite conversion, not the normal Chance roll: it drains 30 Ling per dt, accumulates GoldEffectSpeed per dt using live preparation/environment factors, and ends when Ling is empty. Normal Gold leave forces m_bDid true, calls MakeGold, records quality/grade and adds 0.015 times accumulated quality to energy capacity before clearing the bottleneck. This also banks current accumulated quality on interrupted leave in the reviewed code; exact zero-duration/cancellation ordering is unobserved.

Retained core quality affects more than its display. MakeGold alters NpcLingMaxValue; GlodDanEffectBroken selects a grade-dependent multiplier for later breakthroughs with a separate post-stage-9 table column. GoldLevel ranking runs 1 through 9 with grade 1 at the highest configured quality threshold, so higher quality must not be described as a larger grade number.

Outside RPG mode, expiry can automatically start the owned JobBrokenNeck; action incapacity/selected suppression states adjust or defer the countdown. Thunder/God jobs cannot be interrupted, while Chance/Gold normal jobs are not marked noninterruptible here.

Environment has implementation-backed meaning: light uses a biome/time curve and LightAddP; the seasonal phase is year-day minus ten wrapped over eight annual segments; weather applies/unapplies map-property values. Active XML samples set Overcast ShuiBroken +0.02, LightRain ShuiBroken +0.02 / HuoBroken -0.04, HeavyRain ShuiBroken +0.03 / HuoBroken -0.06. These are modifiers, not full success probabilities.

report_summary: **Finite static source pass complete.** Cult of the Lamb is useful for connecting people, home work, expeditions and institutional identity in YAIR. This pass preserved the supplied rules privately and traced **47 findings across 16 connected paths**, including actual spending, state changes, timing, failure and later consumers. Three original proposals are selected for a future assignment; they do not replace the larger findings or authorize implementation.

The prior [scouting chat](codex://threads/01a1137a-37c6-77e1-8150-b0c007c1330f) established a recommendation without inspecting a build. This dossier is its downloaded-source follow-through. It does not rewrite that chat or claim a whole-game reconstruction.

finding_and_opportunity_index.label: Follower state is resolved before task selection. Disease, injury, intoxication, childhood, exhaustion, cold and exceptional body/trait states have distinct precedence; they are not interchangeable mood labels.

Ordinary tasks drain rest and food and change individual conditions; disease, injury and dissent use different rates. Fasting and cursed states alter food policy. Food and dissent rates are multiplied by0.7 while the player is away from base.

Trait lookup combines personal traits with cult-wide traits, while another info-level lookup reads the personal list alone. Adding a trait removes declared exclusive traits and may immediately clear or add thoughts and bodily states.

Daily advancement resets named interaction claims, ages followers and handles distinct old-age, immortal and child branches. Housing thoughts distinguish facility quality and materialistic reactions; unattended children can leave neglect thoughts.

Personal thoughts have groups, stack limits and per-stack expiry. Expiry can cause later illness or old-age task changes. However the current Happiness getter is constant 50 and its change handler is empty; these thoughts do not establish a working general mood-stat simulation.

Reconsideration releases old reservations, resolves personal priorities, tries to keep an existing unique task, then claims eligible tasks by role/priority category. The shared location scheduler can displace lower-priority allocations and then settles pending choices. The named level-requirement helper currently returns true.

Refinery enqueue removes actual ingredients and stores output type/variant. An assigned worker reserves the refinery and advances its saved progress using productivity. Completion deposits actual stored output and removes the queue head. Removing a queued recipe returns ingredients; removing the active head resets progress.

Farming reserves the station, current plot operation and selected seed/fertilizer stores separately. Refund methods return carried seeds or fertilizer to their original silo and clear carried stock, with explicit missing-silo early exits.

Placement checks current affordability, spends construction ingredients and creates a build site. Worker slots are separately claimed; productivity advances site progress. Completion replaces the build site with the target facility while carrying its inventory, queue and occupant references forward, and creates trait-qualified thoughts.

Community faith combines a clamped persistent base value with tracked thought modifiers. Thoughts replace by group or stack with individual cooldowns; expiration changes the displayed total. Temporary and permanent effects therefore differ.

Low community faith can select an eligible follower after cadence/onboarding/day-phase checks. Loyalty necklaces, bishops, zombies, snowmen and mutation branches limit dissent. A low global value does not turn every follower into a dissenter at once.

Listening to a speaking dissenter requires nearby contact and a per-pair elapsed-time check. Listening can add a personal thought; the listener task includes a Happiness>=80 counterargument branch, but the selected current getter is constant 50.

A dissenter stores a warning and planned theft amount before leaving. The visible departure removes no more than current gold. Its original person record joins a dissented list and can later become a named dungeon enemy; death moves that same record to dead history.

Disciple reeducation reduces a target counter, doubles the reduction for an imprisoned target and records the receiver ID in a daily list. Crossing to zero removes dissent, resolves a cure objective and produces a community thought. Daily list clearing and treatment outcome are separate joins.

The current level-up routine clears adoration and increments level without a cap check; CanLevelUp checks adoration alone. A leftover IsMaxLevel method still returns level >= 10 but has no caller in the exported code search. Loyalty and sin have different thresholds.

Productivity uses a level contribution clamped at10 and then trait, relationship, institution and season modifiers. Missionary success uses its own level tiers; demon effectiveness separately clamps level at10 plus a necklace bonus. The productivity winter-body conditional has a negative false branch even if the trait is absent.

Discipleship requires an available follower of at least level 10 who is not already a disciple, plus ritual availability/affordability. The ceremony explicitly grants the trait/status and increments the created count; reaching the level alone is not this promotion.

Doctrine unlocks are recorded once and drive collective traits or specific ritual/building abilities. Collective traits remove conflicting personal traits and are consulted by actual work, food and winter consumers. This source treats cult policy as authority over members.

Current ritual UI checks unlocked/maxed/cooldown/affordability and specific candidate requirements. Normal successful completion charges UpgradeSystem costs; cancelled and forced branches differ. Promotion and resurrection list a 150-bone base recipe before discounts. Completion also clears the next-free flag and can cause night disruption.

Resurrection removes the selected identity from dead/imprisoned collections, clears its actual grave/crypt/morgue occupancy and recreates the visible follower from the same person data. It resets stats through a helper and extends life expectancy.

After day20, resurrection without a funeral can produce zombie or existential-dread aftermath, with a special Sozo exception. Dread changes the post-ceremony task instead of simply adding a negative description.

Healing checks the selected person cost against actual inventory and removes those items. Costs differ for illness, zombie, mutation and distress and by facility tier. It clears named conditions/traits; mutation removal additionally needs the corresponding doctrine, so spend and complete cure are not identical.

Stored-food work reserves a real meal, ends when the reserved item cannot be eaten and removes the food at arrival. Interrupting while already doing still resolves eating. Satiation overflow is redistributed to other eligible followers, an abstract communal policy rather than per-person nutrition conservation.

Recipe definitions and meal effects are separate. Effects draw independently; some dangerous meals use a special death-versus-loot branch. Food can cure specific states, alter loyalty, add traits or change age. Doctrines, onboarding and heavyweight traits modify these results.

Social contact requires nearby eligible people and task freedom. A conversation is scored across turns, modifies a shared pair record and can cross friends/lovers/enemies thresholds. Parent/sibling and specific-person exceptions block lover transitions; dispositions modify positive talk chance.

Fight aftermath records the aggressor and reason, can kill or injure the victim, rewards a surviving winner and changes thoughts. The delayed result rechecks interruption before committing. Jealous-spouse branches use different risks.

Mating eligibility excludes children, siblings, parent-child pairs and some named/body cases. Relationship, traits, exhaustion, illness and daily seeded variation affect the chance; a story objective can force it. The attempt spends sin before resolution, and the first positive-chance attempt has a special guarantee. These responses are game mechanics, not a general consent model.

Egg data retains parent IDs/names/appearance, seed and selected traits, with golden/unique/mutated/body exceptions and an additional failure flag. Parent trait pools exclude named traits. Hatching updates parent calculations, creates a child and applies specific cult doctrines; daily care has a neglect route.

Missionary dispatch stores person-specific departure time, duration, objective type, chance and facility association, then changes the person task/location. Success is determined before return. Its rules consider level, exhaustion, intoxication and named mission traits; special guaranteed-success states are consumed/reset separately.

At the due boundary, a mission stores real rewards or none and enters a return task. The completed interaction either adds resources to normal inventory or produces a recruit; failure has a return death path. Settlement clears rewards, facility membership and mission occupancy.

Successful returning missionaries become exhausted and may acquire inspired, excited or terrified traits after the introductory days. Those traits change later mission chance and bodily/task behavior; paid healing can remove the distress trait.

Demon assignment occupies actual follower IDs in a summoner and moves them into a task that blocks normal task changes, sermons and thoughts. Ordinary demons are chosen deterministically from identity; unique and mutated people have special roles. Missing facilities or cleared membership restore ordinary tasks.

A demon reads the actual follower’s capped effective level; the selected shooter changes its attack and bomb cooldowns and has a telegraph/recovery sequence. Normal run completion clears demon membership; restoring the person adds exhaustion and repeat-use history when the facility survives.

Run results distinguish escape, death and completion, with difficulty/fleece and shrine/sandbox exceptions. Result adjustments mutate both run stock and inventory. Quest-target resources can be excluded from loss; fragile loot is separately removed. A GameOver path is another domain and calls save-slot deletion, unlike ordinary killed/escaped settlement.

The normal simulation uses frame delta converted to game time and visits active and unloaded follower representations. Skipping time is an explicit path. Normal colony work can continue during a crusade; the accessibility StopTimeInCrusade option instead pauses the simulation manager. UI pause, simulation pause and PauseGameTime are distinct controls. No browser-closed or OS-offline policy was established.

Active winter with exhausted warmth can select a follower to freeze after severity/grace/cadence checks. Blizzard and trait branches change cadence. Personal protection, scarf, exceptional body, traits and necklace qualify cold exposure. Winter also has facility snow-cover and spatial heating-range rules.

Fuel insertion spends an actual item and uses its weight up to facility capacity. Winter simulation drains furnace fuel and gives bounded low/empty warnings. A declared upgrade can refill on seasonal entry; another lock suppresses burn. Furnace waste can occupy a real nearby place.

Ranch animals age and change need/readiness on phases. Away from base, low satiation takes actual trough food; adult growth readiness is suppressed by overcrowding, milk readiness resets separately, and selected older unprotected animals can die. Player-animal and riding/leashed branches differ.

Animal work produces species-specific materials; milk is separate. Work consumes readiness and sets a daily flag. Ordinary feeding deducts an item, but special feed can change ailments and schedule a fight; a feral branch can return before the ordinary deduction. Meat output also changes under feral state.

Ranch capacity comes from real enclosure tiles. Mating moves the actual parents into a hutch until a target phase, supports detachment/abort and creates one fresh-ID child whose appearance, speed and favorite food depend on both parents. The full riding/speed consumer and fence-search algorithm are outside this pass.

An assigned rancher respects player reservations, cleans or works actual animals, carries produced material in its own inventory and later deposits it in ranch storage before clearing cargo. The offscreen branches operate on saved animal data and differ from visible animation callbacks.

Woolhaven shrine offerings check and spend actual stock and advance distinct unlock stages. Ghost deposit removes inventory before a tracked in-air delivery, then increments received/total progress. Thresholds can advance winter severity, unlock later access and introduce additional pressures such as blizzards and buried structures, with boss-completion exceptions.

Pilgrim quests require the pack flag, named people, prior acceptance, elapsed days and actual discoveries. Stages create protected objectives, recruits/searches and a bag recovery. Completion unlocks bonus comic pages through persistent data; a stage-two repair rechecks actual objectives/recruited IDs before retaining acceptance. The comic prose and whole quest graph were not read.

Follower data declares keyed identity/location/task destination/home, mission commitments, rewards, parentage, inventory, traits, funeral history and pair relationships. Loaded and simulated follower objects share the brain/data model; visible entity replacement is not a new person. These are selected static definitions, not a save roundtrip audit.

Some convincing names are dormant or simplified in this build: GetXP is empty, GetDevotionGeneration returns zero, Happiness is constant 50, and RequiredFollowerLevel returns true. The export also has a repeated missionary-tier condition and conditional modifier asymmetries. Successful export and readable names are not equivalent to intended or tested behavior.

The supplied base payload includes Woolhaven and Pilgrim implementation classes and packaged DLC definitions. Woolhaven activation checks Steam subscription for app3840050 in the normal static route; source presence therefore does not establish activation or ownership. No entitlement check was executed. Cosmetic/music classification is based on the official catalog, with packaged historical bonus metadata separate.

Some spatial rules are real mechanics: follower interaction distance, habitat tile capacity and heating coverage qualify outcomes. Other presentation work merely reflects data or delivers a callback. The code distinguishes active, loaded and unloaded locations, but full pathfinding, room prefabs and serialized defaults remain unread.

finding_and_opportunity_index.label: Entangling is a weighted weapon brand and a polearm-related choice. A successful brand branch rolls coinflip and checks can_constrict before storing attacker/victim IDs and hold type. A resistant or already-held victim is excluded; entangling requires reach and at most one entangling target. Hold validity depends on actual actor life, line of sight and range; moving farther away can break direct holds. Continuing damage applies half-AC handling, timescale and hurt/death consequences. Noita's useful lesson is to keep **material identity, physical properties,
contents and use route separate**. The same oil can burn on the floor,
protect a stained body and cause a different effect when swallowed. Spells
work as a small interpreter with shared cast groups and nested payloads,
so a modifier is more than a bonus attached to the next card.

The owned install finished successfully. I extracted and hash-checked its
readable data without launching it. This pass covers 468 material records,
330 active reaction records, 422 spell actions and 106 perks. Counts cover
the catalogues; detailed reading covers the specific systems listed in
[COVERAGE.json](COVERAGE.json). Native engine behavior remains qualified.

finding_and_opportunity_index.label: 468 material definitions with inheritance, numeric physics and explicit special hooks, not a universal property-only system.
330 active authored reaction records: identity and family selectors, higher arity, requirements, geometry and entity outputs. E4 needs adapters rather than direct copying.
No active Lua/XML generator found; community tool reconstructs seed-resolved LC and AP recipes. Binary equivalence not tested.
Modifiers share a cast group; triggers compile fresh child groups from a shared deck/mana budget before impact.
Perks rewrite personal response/emission; fungal shift is TRIP-driven world conversion with no Lua expiry. Stack availability differs from mathematical composition.

Materials attach contact statuses through legacy status_effects or structured Stains. OILED, like WET, is marked as fire protection on the body; loose oil is burnable. The summary that oil feeds fire must distinguish loose fuel from coating.

Ingestion has its own per-material dose/effect rows. A useful stain may be harmful when drunk: invisibility liquid gives FOOD_POISONING by ingestion. Solids also have ingestion effects, so neither every liquid having an effect nor every material being consumable follows.

Status data has tiers rather than a uniform stack: INGESTION_DRUNK thresholds are 0, 0.25, 0.75 and 1, with POISONED added at 1. TRIP has four tiers; CURSE_CLOUD three. Effects carry finite frame durations and may have exclusivity groups.

Flasks hold mixtures indexed by material type and run reactions inside the inventory. The ordinary flask sucks up to barrel_size 1000 and enables reaction chance 20, explosions and entity outputs. Powder pouch has material_type 1, barrel_size 1500 and drinkable 0. One-material containers are an explicit YAIR simplification, not the observed Noita model.

Standard polymorph targets sheep for 600 frames and random polymorph uses the RANDOM target. Engine documentation exposes serialized original entity storage. A mass polymorph script targets both homing targets and player units, with boss and immunity exclusions. Restoring memories or a soul is YAIR design, not a Noita source fact.

Players, basic enemies and animals share damage/status component families, but authored parameters differ. Enemy AI has herd relations and aggression, not only tag matching. The directed relation matrix has 35 herds and 133 asymmetric unordered pairs. Shared mechanics do not imply identical susceptibility or universal friendly fire.

Orb pickups separate first discovery from later encounters: a first encounter creates a spell card from storage, a known orb creates a heart, and out-of-bounds orb IDs create evil hearts. Tablet offerings convert physical tablets to gold and repeated offerings may spawn monsters. These are concrete knowledge, place and history gates. Claims about community discovery dates are not established by the install.

DiscoveryTree uses persisted offer state: action mode/time, rerolls, excluded/current IDs, rarity levels, selected ID and OrbRandom survive ordinary save/load. It initializes item pools from discoverList, splits required items, and restores the RNG from its saved state/global salt.

Its paid discover click precedes three seconds of crafting; a separate selected-item confirmation then settles discovery. Choice mode does not advance on elapsed time.

Required visible discoveries supersede random offers. Other offers are undiscovered+visible items; the algorithm guarantees ready candidates when available and can include future-use candidates, weighted by remaining prerequisite distance. Confirmation discovers one item, clears the offer, increments cost counts; reroll consumes a saved charge, excludes the former offer and recrafts. Empty offers fall back to idle. Nonchosen rarity enhancements are removed; chosen rarity remains.

Ritual discovery requires recipe-book availability, all prerequisite rituals discovered, and discover requirements. It can be offered before its usage prerequisites are satisfied, because those separately supply discovery-range distance; unmet usage increases activation cost and shows an insufficient-state warning.

Ritual activation enters real wave combat. Ongoing resource drain fills completion slots; enemy death weight also fills slots by spending currently available resources. Full completion requires at least five waves plus fully filled slots. Player death ends the run; a run is classed failed only below five waves, independently of the full-completion predicate.

End grants instant rewards proportional to waves even before the early-failure branch. Failure refunds raw activationCost times one minus the player fail penalty and exits before duration/permanent rewards or completion events. Success installs duration instances, updates highest reached level, raises completion events, and reapplies permanent effects scaled from the highest reach. Permanent means current-run persistent effects, not NG+ retention: RitualSO lacks IPersistentReset and ResetData clears discovery/reach/instances/effects.

Duration instances carry level/power/duration; reload reinitializes and reapplies their player status effects. They expire from played-time increments and remove associated modifiers. Non-echo active instances influence repeated-activation penalties and chain length for later rituals.

Research has separate capacity use and consumed development resources. UIResearchItem disables cost-button payment; Develop/Queue applies researchCost as keyed resource usage, while totalCost fills by resource drain. Insufficient supply lowers drain ratio and progress. Queue selects affordable/legal future levels and continuation starts after level completion. Cancel clears investment and queue; pause retains the investment. Reached levels enable prerequisite links and apply persistent reward blocks.

The actual time-screen reset route requires complete-world-cycle and fetched challenges. Initial challenge fetch is free; later rerolls require positive reroll tokens and consume one. CompleteWorldCycle completes active finish-the-game challenges, refills rerolls, marks world complete, and adds a two-point pending-cycle contribution to starting time advancements. Serialized WorldComplete is raised by the final Restoration ritual and routed through listener11406.

Persistent reset captures each saveable IPersistentReset object only when its IsPersistent() is true, resets it, reloads its captured state and invokes its callback; all other IResetable objects reset. Global seed is salted. Then manager clears completed/fetched flags, retains last persistence value, clears cycle timer, activates pending rewards/new challenges, increments reset count, derives persistent-resource maximum from last persistence, and reloads the scene without ordinary full reset.

Time runes always enter the retain/reload path, but their callback then clears current level, discovered flag and rarity. Mastery level/XP and seen flag survive; mastery consumers are reapplied to player and rune types on initialization. Research persists only when any assigned ResearchType has persistThroughReset. Achievements, challenges and keybindings always return persistent; advancement/number variables depend on asset isPersistent flags; number variables additionally need saveValue to emit saved state.

Challenges retain earned level/state. Specific goals can pass while playing; finish-the-game goals pass when WorldComplete calls CompleteGame. Failure removes current restrictions without advancing level. The actual time-screen Button13504 -> event5070 -> listener17046 -> UITimeScreenManager17107.FetchNewChallenges uses modern ChallengeManager.GenerateNewChallengeList, with compulsory increased-difficulty, weighted types, incompatible/excluded entries and probabilistic preferred entries. The exported legacy modal6292 and PersistentResetManager.FetchNewChallenges contain a deprecated generator path; it is not the reviewed active time-screen route.

Live simulation runs in FixedUpdate with fixedDeltaTime and slow increments every 0.2 seconds. Save load restores state and played time; save-age timestamp is calculated for a variable. No reviewed managed startup/load consumer passes elapsed save age into game simulation, and searches found no game offline/catch-up routine or application-focus/pause hook. This supports no managed catch-up path found, not a whole-installed-game/runtime proof of no offline progress or background behavior.

Automation is explicit and funded: AutoBuy only scans trivial affordable structures after an empty action queue and positive enabled queue capacity, using a five-second timer modified by speed. AutoPurchase instances use engaged resource drains and four times base build time, increase structure quantity then reengage at next cost, and expose removal/refund. This is supported live automation, not evidence of closed-app accrual.

Plot nodes offer another live background path: optional automatic action instances, natural growth only with enough space-use capacity, timed Growing/Resting phases, mastery from active work, and distinct consuming versus exiting/resting actions. Actual late-world species/nodes and numerical growth are serialized content; species catalogue outside the selected chain remains unread.

Actual base discovery options are two; base banked rerolls are zero until rewards improve them. Ritual Discoveries3258 is based on Ceremony costs with Expert Mystic3653 reducing cost; Restoration and Surrender are required discoveries with their own discoverCost, so they bypass the random pool when their prerequisites become visible. The retained Restore the World achievement grants one discovery-reroll capacity by a NumberVariable effect.

All eleven extracted ResearchTypeSO persistThroughReset flags are false, including the type named Enduring. Thus the reviewed research-type condition retains no research. Of 48 advancement templates, all 28 non-time fruit/plot/stone advancements have isPersistent=0, while all 20 time advancements4813–4832 have isPersistent=1. Names like permanent or enduring are not enough to establish reset retention.

Restoration upgrade4380 needs Death Stone4365 level>0 and Beacon3889 visibility, and costs authored base8e43 Ceremony plus1e24 Beacon. The required Restoration ritual3933 needs that upgrade and all Life/Death/Principle recipe books; it costs authored discovery1e38 Knowledge, activation100 Zeal, has forceLevel70 and five base waves, with Beacon/Cognitive Disc/Organic Essence completion resources subject to its actual completion-level scaling3471. Its reward lists are empty; its onCompleteEvents raises WorldComplete3380, which calls cycle completion and the finale animation/modal. These are static content definitions, not current player progress or unmodified end-user quotes.

Successful casting grants SurrenderPassive3516. A CharacterDeath reaction with100% base chance, zero cooldown and no active character-type filter executes Gain Divine Fragments3892. Character.Die fires Player passive checks; consumed fragments plus Hexsteel3895 pay Death Stone4365, which follows Life Stone4366 and enables Restoration upgrade. Surrender expiry/cancel removes its attached passive by actual GUID, stopping that production path. Content prose mentions aberrations, but the reviewed condition is inactive, so the source trigger is broader.

Retained TimeRune mastery is reconstructed into Total Time Rune Mastery5651 on initialization. Player observes this number and applies its effects with bonusLevels1; its active effect contributes one Starting Time Advancement5645 per total mastery level. The manager snapshots the resulting starting advancements at reset and applies it to Time Advancement3855 capacity. Rune current levels then reserve this shared capacity through keyed usage, so past mastery changes the budget for later current-cycle rune allocations.

Advancement Persist rune5470 levels by using Time Advancement capacity and executes instant GainXp into persistent Advancement Boost4814 before its current level increments. Discovery of a future-use ritual can also carry a separate duration penalty when usage requirements are unmet. The nonfailure End path raises WorldComplete. Full completion and end-event success therefore use different predicates. This is a possible correctness gap and runtime-unverified alternate aftermath, not a tested exploitation claim or a model YAIRPG should copy.

The enabled Time screen17107 controls actual Button16672 -> PersistentReset5075 -> listener11405 -> manager reset. Button13504 -> new-challenge event5070 -> listener17046 -> time-screen FetchNewChallenges selects the modern challenge generator. Time screen visibility is gated by TimeResetUnlocked3605, an OR of world-reset count>=1 or WorldCycleComplete3609 (Restoration reached>=1). The extracted ordinary number flags set Attributes Developed5664 and Spells Casted5689 to saveValue1/isPersistent1. World Reset count4587 and Previous Time Advancements5646 are saveable but not persistent by flag; PersistentResetManager explicitly captures/reinstates their values while incrementing the reset count. The two-way distinction between generic retention flags and manager restoration matters.

Plots retain separate Idle, Growing and Resting populations. Action usage reserves eligible Idle units unless useAnyStateForCost is true. Plants occupy space across phases. Empty land follows missing plot capacity and enters 40-second serial recovery, so destroying a tree does not immediately make all its land usable. GetTotalUsageCost excludes erraticQuantity; the selected tree assets have hasErraticGrowth=false, so their path does not establish a universal natural-spawn cost.

The selected chain consumes 2 empty units for 1 Oak, 2 Oaks for 1 Force tree, and 2 Force trees for 1 Ironwood. Idle parents stay reserved during paid work. Completion creates the target in Growing and then consumes parents. Occupied space conserves 2, 4 and 8 units. Base capacity 8 fits one Ironwood, while auxiliary moss or a spring needs more space.

CreateWorldPillar opens agromancy. Energize requires purchased Energy Trees; Imbue requires purchased Ironwood Trees; fruit requires purchased Create Fruit Trees; treasure requires completed Treasure Trees research. A link tier and its paid acquisition are distinct. These notes inspect those gates, not the full progression leading to them.

Fuel is a continuous drain rather than an up-front prepaid total. Timer progress is maxed action speed multiplied by ResourceDrain support. The least-supported input slows or stalls work; other drains scale with that bottleneck. Growing and Resting phases advance independently at their own speed.

Base action time differs from maturation and actual time. Parent size, quality and optional space rarity change duration; the speed clamp limits completion to at most once per second. Selected planting and tree conversions run serially, while their resulting Growing timers run in parallel.

Ironwood harvesting drains nominal 50 Skill per second and applies a persistent raw Ironwood rate of 0.002 through HarvestScaling during work. It destroys one tree at completion and has no completion lump output. Fruit and treasure collection instead have no action effects or drain and call a treasure pool only on completion.

Cancel clears all durations and action quantity, then removes fuel drains, effects and usage. If actionEffects is empty, reserved parents become available again, but spent fuel is not refunded. A persistent harvest spends one element-cost batch and rotates or destroys its size because output has already accrued; other reserved units are released. Cancellation is not a universal resource refund.

Force bark has two policies: destroy one Force tree for ongoing Wood and ForceBark during nominal 16-second harvesting, or pay 14 Skill per second for nominal 32-second peeling, which moves one Force tree to Resting for 45 seconds serially and then Growing for 240 seconds in parallel. Fruit and treasure also retain occupancy through recovery and regrowth.

Fruit uses three Oaks and six occupied plot units; treasure uses three Force trees and twelve units. Collection calls EarnPartialTreasure, which retains fractional rewards. Weighted eligible content reaches ConsumableSO.Gain. The Fruit item groups and Core subpools differ; a specific item is not guaranteed.

Non-growing completions trigger node-type consumeEffects, including rating-based Plant Core treasure. Growing tree conversions skip those effects. Refund-rating echoes can add completions without consuming a parent each time. Exact random outcomes remain unverified.

Enrich is a competing sink: it consumes three trees and sends 10 scaled XP to a named Advancement, rather than producing harvest stock or a growing replacement. Its raw duration of 1e-5 seconds still faces the one-second speed clamp. Downstream Advancement progression remains unread.

Unreserved Idle moss supplies a raw Verdant rate of 0.16 and a NaturalResourceType GainRate modifier. A water spring occupies five plots and supplies Water plus PlantNodeType GrowingSpeed and Yield modifiers. Reserving units for work suppresses passive contribution through GetRemainingQuantity. Material, growing speed, yield and occupied capacity remain distinct roles.

Ironwood has an actual alchemy consumer: discovered Extract Ironwood reserves Mechanical capacity and drains nominal 0.012 Ironwood per second. It supplies functional capacity modifiers of 4 Alchemical, 16 Biotic and 8 Occultic units. These are not direct Organic or Occult Essence outputs or input fuel refunds.

ExpertAlchemy level 16 is an Extract Ironwood soft usage condition. Its last core type, Alchemy, defines unmet penalties of double usage, quarter speed, sixteen-fold cost and a 0.97 effect-scaling exponent. Discovery, affordability and full support are separate. The nominal 0.012 drain is not a universal live quote.

Functional capacity effects do not multiply their quoted max modifier by the support ratio. ResourceSO writes that ratio into usageDrainPenalty. Functional max becomes part of nominal capacity, while consumer ResourceDrains propagate the support ratio. Starvation can leave nominal capacity visible while reducing downstream work. Disengaging removes functional modifiers, reservations and drains; spent Ironwood stays spent.

An enabled AutoBuyManager binding exists in level1. Its five-second timer, scaled by speed, runs only with an empty general Actionable list, positive queue size and enabled flag. It scans AllStructures in order, checks availability, level requirements, room and trivial cost, forces single purchases, and queues real construction. Trivial means each true price is less than stock divided by 1000. This manager does not choose or automate agromancy chains.

Assets include debug-like phase quantities, sizes and hasBeenUsed flags. ResetData clears plot quantities, mastery, visibility and modifiers, and clears the action-used flag. These serialized values do not establish a fresh profile or runtime state.

A target without a condition manager also fails closed.

ColdSnap adds a -20 C temperature offset ramped over 12,000 ticks. The manager aggregates applicable condition offsets (including parent/world conditions), and TileTemperaturesComp adds that offset to cached outdoor temperature. Plant.GrowthRateFactor_Temperature reads actual cell temperature and passes it to plant temperature growth rules. The condition manager serializes active conditions, reconnects their manager on load, ticks them, and ends expired conditions.

report_summary: **Section F is complete as a targeted read-only source audit of build 25598304.** The installed-data pass is reconciled with the earlier text findings. No gameplay was changed or tested.

**F31/F44-F46, seen in data or code:** company management combines counted crew, real consumption, wages, cargo and staffing. Different beasts make different logistics trade-offs; shortages sharply reduce travel capacity. Named companions are separate records with roles, growth and particular reactions.

finding_and_opportunity_index.label: Bulk workforce and named companion/deputy roles are different abstractions. Staffing shortages reduce movement. Temporary, fixed-Prowess hirelings need not have personal stories.
Event tests distinguish the leader alone, selected companions, and the whole company through icons/tooltips.
Enslaved crew have an Obedience system distinct from free crew morale. Guard ratios, food, new captives and choices affect it; escapes and theft are possible.

Named-companion quests require that companion, award trust and Insight, and gate Prowess milestones. Branches and rewards are unequal. The launch notes say personal stories shipped for all nine then-available companions.

Developers reported that hidden automatic outpost supply buying made upkeep appear onerous. Players in one thread call loyalty notifications distracting, while others find gifts and quests sufficient.
The pre-alpha camp resolves one-day turns with owed wages, supply consumption, crew changes, banter, healing and paid rest or defenses; nighttime events can follow End Day.
The documented camp allows wage postponement or a double-wage promise, and next-day rations affect vigor/morale.
Work demand includes care of beasts, loading, cooking and camp tasks. Low morale/obedience and crew loss reduce supply of labor. A deficit below half demand is a more severe movement penalty.
Historical foraging uses workers or enslaved workers at camp and resolves at end of day; regional yield, vigor and Survival affect tests. Worker injury/loss or escape are possible.
Historical hunting uses scouts, region, Hunting and a Venatoris deputy; it can lose scouts and return secondary loot. Revealing yield through scouting was still a proposal in this article.
The in-house Event Editor connects steps, choices, dependencies and consequences with map, settlement and camp triggers; it also authors journal and codex dependencies.
Loyalty feedback can be Off, Basic direction, or Indicative magnitude. A patch renamed the top tier Loyal.
The 1.165 notes increase Gor’Goro’s early quest loyalty and add gift options, while Eylani loses loyalty for fighting beasts in Kabur’s arena.
A player reports Gor’Goro threatening departure after a slavery-related choice; others report no departures with gifts/quests.
Assigning a deputy adds daily upkeep; removing a deputy that grants equipment capacity now refreshes slots immediately.

Historical Authority controls deputy capacity; Resourcefulness refreshes per turn and buys specific actions. Shared Insight funds leader improvements or companion Prowess; attributes gate trait/skill purchases.
Regular faction gains can antagonize rivals. One-time prizes differ from standing-dependent boons that disappear when standing falls and can be reclaimed locally.
Sunfire and Moonshadow describes regional nemesis pairs with an irreversible allegiance threshold, unlike usually repairable regular faction relations.
Mercenary task timers now stop at narrative completion, not eventual return to the issuer, including successful defense.
A scouting rework describes area coverage, more scouts reducing movement cost, lower success with broader coverage, a Resourcefulness guarantee for one category, and results retained for three days.

Historical healing uses rest, profession, accommodation and medical supplies; injuries restrict the vitality ceiling and improve by stages. A failed natural heal can worsen condition but is bounded at one vitality.
The developer deliberately chose manual saving and replaying quests, and says the game was not designed as a roguelike.
These sources support companion attitudes and continued company play but do not establish an implemented generational successor/loyalty transfer system.

Iona already has funded/personal teaching terms and solo patrol state; Lio has owned kit, stamina and effort; actor relationships have distinct axes, causal receipts and bounded memories; Tamsin has her own response plan.

Original Frontier has actual dispatcher/receiver purses, reserved physical cargo, declared cancellation and native journey progress. Earlier guide work already varies duration/reward by guide and crossing condition.
The source UI still says fresh body, one lesson, while accepted direction is inheritance of what was actually left behind.
AddLoyalty does nothing in Pilgrims of the Wasteland, for hirelings, missing character records or alignment zero. Simulated execution only reports eligibility.

Altruistic/Kind/Cruel/Malevolent choices select eight-position alignment arrays. Eligible present/selected companions get the indexed change; negative changes are scaled by (11-Authority)/10 and rounded. Positive changes are not scaled here.

Loyalty thresholds are -100,-25,0,80,200,400,750, producing tiers -2 through 4; scores below -100 return -3. Display merges tiers below -1 as Resentful and tiers above 2 as Loyal. GetMin/MaxLoyalty refers to -1000/1000 defaults.

A character removal action can be scheduled by in-game day. Removal clears roster/enemy membership, role assignment and formations, invalidates dependent sources, and unmounts gear/perks. UnmountAll clears mount references without removing the holder’s gear slots.

Crew rows contain upkeep, consumption, cargo, movement/march base, workforce and need. Total consumption/upkeep sum crew-category properties; workforce uses rounded 100-times row coefficient times count, with passengers handled separately. Named companions contribute through character records.
Staffing evaluates total workforce/need. Non-easy mode checks inclusive intervals 0.5-1, 0.12-0.5, 0-0.12; easy mode uses 0.3-0.75, 0.05-0.3, 0-0.05.

Camp sums existing upkeep arrears plus current promised pay, with double wages multiplying the current promise. Paying debits money, clears accrued crew entries and resets unpaid days; an unpaid camp increments the day counter.

Displayed supply days use integer supplies/total consumption, substituting divisor one at zero consumption. Rated consumption rounds total consumption times ration percentage. At an outpost it can withdraw available stock before debiting supplies.

EndCamp handles pay, defensive cost, ration/rest impacts, optional encouragement, crew ledgers and supplies; its continuation executes hunting/foraging and can run an end-camp event before finalizing the day.

Tests pass leader-only and selected-hero flags into perk aggregation. Assigned caravan roles have a special selection check; companion perks can sum or take the highest. CountTotalPerkLevel adds company perks when not restricted to a nonempty selected subset.

Choices contain dependencies, tests, combat, next/success/fail/end/auto actions and hero selection. The parser routes dependency, test and result commands; execution merges explicit loyalty changes with alignment reactions.

Companion upkeep combines the character’s base pay, a (Prowess-1)*2 increment unless a particular status excludes it, and five per assigned role. Certain statuses or changed Gor’Goro return zero upkeep; Sedarias has zero consumption in this method.

GetElapsedDays uses a finished timestamp when present. Ready-success tasks use max(fail,success) stamps; other tasks use max(fail,complete). Delivery classification compares this elapsed time with Fast/Ontime/Late limits.

Container claims reject an already-claimed tier/container and apply its goods once. Status claims track the reward but can re-add a missing status. Tier changes remove statuses from rewards above the new tier.
IsDefeatedByNemesis checks an opponent at tier four or above; AddReputation then returns without changing reputation.

Plain StreamingAssets/eventdata/build.json contains 46 base-event and 569 subevent records with reference-linked nodes. PoolLoader separately loads encrypted Addressables text tables for events, journals/codex and core Airtable data.

Character state serializes identity, health/vitality/power, asset path, perk/skill records, properties and statuses. Choice history stores day, step and choice index; event history stores day, event and node IDs.

Workers and enslaved crew both have workforce coefficient 0.9. A worker consumes two supplies, carries six cargo and costs one base upkeep unit after the loader multiplies monetary fields by 100. The enslaved row consumes one supply, carries nine cargo and has zero wage.
Insectoid/reptile/mammal burden beasts respectively consume 9/16/12, carry 400/400/350 and need 4.5/2.8/3.7 workforce; their base movement is 8/9/8.
The three staffing statuses point to modifiers of -25% movement/-25% march, -50% movement/-40% march, and -95%/-95%.

GetMaxCharProwess starts at 3, then completed character-specific journal milestones raise the cap to 5, 7 and 9. A trusted-tester branch bypasses this to 9. The UI uses the cap in upgrade availability.

Fourteen low-loyalty event records require tier at least -2 and not at least -1, with 30-40-day repeat frequency and priority classification. For the standard tier function this is score -100 through -26. Their reviewed responses end the conversation.

Eleven critical events require tier at least -3 and not at least -2, corresponding to score below -100, and use highpriority classification. Hidden journal-specific branches remove the character and may fail an assigned quest; selected Nedir branches remove an item or gear, while selected Garrik/Skornar/Finndurarth branches remove particular passengers or quest items.

The oil gift requires an owned oil unit and 30-day cadence, removes one oil and adds 15 loyalty. One-time gift alternatives use max-count gates. Other banter options vary with loyalty tier and prior journal/variable evidence; a selected conversation adds two Insight and twelve loyalty.

Treating the injured enslaved worker with supplies requires Healer 4 and one Medical Supplies item, consumes that item, applies a Kind reaction and gives explicit loyalty additions to three named companions. Improvised treatment requires Healer 3 and costs two vigor. Killing reduces enslaved crew by one and applies Cruel. Each branch ends through its own follow-up.
Treatment prose describes days of rest and others working harder; departure prose describes taking provisions and belongings.

A direct event sets the SaltSupply variable for a nearby settlement, independent comitati or selected faction providers. The nearby-settlement option requires an outpost beast or four mounts; some faction choices have standing gates and some are hidden. Leaving without new instructions is an option.

Recovered core data has 12 crew rows, 517 character rows, 88 faction rows, 592 trade task rows and 319 mercenary task rows. The older event table has 1,178 records, 17,223 steps and 34,323 choices; readiness tags are 1,124 ready, four final, 17 progress and 33 idea. New graph data separately has 46 base events/569 subevents.
Gor’Goro, Finndurarth, Harvek and Garrik have alignment entries 3, 1, 7 and 8, respectively, feeding the recovered moral-action arrays. Bespoke event effects supplement these shared categories.

Loyalty is a numeric property with minimum -1000 and a MaxLoyalty reference initialized to 1000. LoyaltyTier is computed and has minimum -3; different negative tiers share Resentful and upper tiers share Loyal display labels.

related_works.title: Elin
observed_facts: The developer describes a roguelike sandbox combining crafting, survival, and base building/management.
The product page lists housing, fishing, music, farming, livestock breeding, childbirth, shops, tourism, companions, and pets among its play options.
The developer describes a mix of generated content and fixed content faithful to its setting.
related_works.inference_and_yair_connection: Useful contrast for letting home, ordinary skills, and local services create more than one life route. Current YAIR owners include village/everyday-life activities, site projects, jobs, native stock, and world instances. The useful question is which one optional home service or profession creates a new capability or visit reason, not whether to add a settlement-management layer.
related_works.limits_and_rights: Store-page feature claims only; no game session, mechanics tracing, save behavior, or content/assets were reviewed. Elin is a commercial game. Use this as a design comparison; do not copy its names, prose, art, code, or setting.

related_works.title: Soulash 2

source_routes.kind: developer-published Steam announcements, including v0.10 Living World and v0.10.3 Economy

observed_facts: The product page describes simulated history, skill-based progression, customizable abilities, material-based crafting, building, and trading; it identifies the title as Early Access.

The developer's Living World announcement describes settlement events with lasting consequences, wilderness events and weather, NPC adventuring groups, and a new world-event data-file type for modders.
The developer's Economy announcement describes a skill whose use unlocks more ways to influence the city, move resources, and direct other workers.
related_works.inference_and_yair_connection: A strong comparator for joining an ordinary skill to settlement influence, funded labor, and off-screen events. YAIR already owns skills, jobs, actors, causes, simulation effects, settlement/site facts, clocks, and publication. A small authored event can reuse these owners; Soulash's autonomous settlement scale is not a required first-milestone system.
related_works.limits_and_rights: Official feature descriptions and announcements only, not code or a playthrough; no claim about the complete event or migration implementation. The work is commercial and Early Access. No code, wording, names, art, or world content is proposed for copying.

related_works.title: Caves of Qud
observed_facts: The product page describes physical simulation, including digging, corrosive mutation, and melting terrain according to material melting points.

The official press kit describes actors with skills, equipment, faction allegiances, and body parts; it gives psionic domination of a spider as an example of inhabiting its body and using its capabilities.
The developer describes more than seventy factions and an authored story woven through physical, social, and historical simulation.
related_works.inference_and_yair_connection: Compare one body/source-specific capability and one environmental interaction at a time. Current YAIR owners include body progression, capabilities and power models, native combat, people/knowledge, and world/situation facts. The connection is a useful counter or passage rule that changes because of the actual actor body or owned faculty, not importing Qud's tile simulation or faction count.
related_works.limits_and_rights: Official descriptions only; no code, full simulation trace, or playthrough. Caves of Qud is commercial. Do not copy its lore, factions, mutation text, artwork, or code.

related_works.title: Dwarf Fortress
observed_facts: The developer describes generated worlds with civilizations, personalities, creatures, cultures, and histories, and inhabitants with simulated personalities.

related_works.title: Wildermyth
observed_facts: The Modding Guide says most game data is JSON, user mods mirror the core game's directory layout, and the in-game Content and Comics Editor exposes events, abilities, aspects, campaigns, items, and monsters.

Story Inputs and Outputs documents checks over campaign/company state, legacy unlocks, present heroes, and other heroes; story roles can be chosen using traits, relationships, hooks, aspects, or stats.

The same guide enumerates supported outcomes including gear, body modifications, history lines, stat changes, hooks/aspects, map changes, relationships, unlocks, recruitment, and combat effects. It recommends clear risk/tradeoffs, permanent visible change for major moments, and mechanically simple supported outcomes.
The Legacy page describes a saved history of accomplishments and heroes, with recruitment in later campaigns preserving selected abilities subject to legacy tier.
related_works.inference_and_yair_connection: The strongest lesson is an authoring contract: declare which campaign and character facts a story may inspect, select relevant roles, then connect a legible choice to a bounded set of supported effects and durable history. YAIR already has source-authored registries, situations, response predicates, validated effects, actors, relationships, attributed knowledge, and saved causes. The missing convenience is an editorial authoring workflow and reusable role/query layer, not another effects engine or a global hero legacy.
related_works.limits_and_rights: Wiki authoring documentation and product design only, not Wildermyth code or complete player experience. No content, JSON files, icons, story text, characters, or assets are proposed for copying. Modding instructions themselves warn authors to contact an existing mod author before adapting and republishing their work.

source_routes.kind: creator's published game and deployed script links
public source directory in the creator-profile GitHub Pages repository

observed_facts: The published interface documents per-clone action queues, synchronization and no-sync commands, repeat actions, zone routes, route estimates, and import/export for queues and saves.

The creator's GitHub profile identifies Sam Benner and links the public GitHub Pages repository. The live page loads named JavaScript modules; the repository additionally exposes the TypeScript source directory. Read-only source inspection confirmed concrete queue/action, clone, route, and zone modules. No scripts were executed.

The repository's LICENSE.md is a custom four-condition BSD-style license. It requires notices and disclaimer retention and says commercial use must first be authorized by Sam Benner or follow a good-faith attempt to obtain permission.
related_works.inference_and_yair_connection: The useful design contrast is visible planned work across coordinated agents and routes. YAIR has jobs, common game clocks, clock leases, simulation commitments, and multi-world boundaries; it does not have clone-level synchronized queues or Cavernous route search. One readable authored preparation plan may be worth comparing, while reproducing queue management would add substantial interface and timing complexity.
related_works.limits_and_rights: Interface evidence is published-page inspection plus the previously qualified entry in docs/NICHE_GAME_REFERENCES.md, not a game playthrough. Source coverage is limited to locating the project and inspecting selected TypeScript files; there was no repo-wide audit, build, execution, install, or gameplay test. Any direct code use needs an explicit license review and the listed commercial-use condition; page-hosted assets and other content were not separately licensed or audited.
